content.title: Education Department Hands Over Federal Student Loans to Treasury
content.text: KEY TAKEAWAYS The Department of Education is beginning the process of moving the trillion-dollar federal student loan portfolio to the Department of the Treasury.Borrowers in active repayment will not experience changes to their loan servicer or payment process. The Department of Education is beginning the process of transferring the management of federal student loans to the Department of the Treasury.1 The Education Department announced on late Thursday that this transition will work in phases. The Department of the Treasury will begin managing part of the portfolio Thursday. Treasury's first order of business will be to collect on defaulted federal student loans and move the currently 9.2 million borrowers in default and 2.4 million in late-stage delinquency back into repayment, a senior Department of Education official and a senior Department of the Treasury official said in a press call with reporters. Student loan borrowers in active repayment will see no change in their loan servicer or how they make payments, senior officials said. Previously, Federal Student Aid, under the Department of Education, with the help of contracted loan servicers, handled the nearly $1.7 billion federal student loan portfolio. This transition moves the Department of Education closer to complete elimination, as President Donald Trump ordered in 2025. The Department of Education had previously debated moving the federal student loan portfolio to a private lender or the Small Business Administration. “The Federal Student Assistance Partnership marks an intentional and historic step toward breaking up the federal education bureaucracy and dramatically improving the administration of federal student aid programs that millions of American students, families, and borrowers rely on to access higher education,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon, in a press release.
